items.title: ACHIEVE-4: oral GLP-1 RA orforglipron is CV-safe vs insulin glargine in high-risk type 2 diabetes (The Lancet)
items.summary: In 2,749 adults with type 2 diabetes, overweight or obesity and established CVD or CKD, once-daily oral orforglipron was non-inferior to insulin glargine for 4-point MACE over a median 2 years (4.2% vs 5.0%; HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.59-1.20). It is the first CV outcomes trial of a non-peptide (small-molecule) GLP-1 receptor agonist; GI side effects were more common and hypoglycaemia less common. (The Lancet, published 30 Sep 2026.)
bullets: **ACHIEVE-4** (Lancet): phase 3, event-driven, **open-label** RCT of **oral non-peptide GLP-1 RA orforglipron vs insulin glargine**.
**2,749 adults** with type 2 diabetes, BMI ≥25, HbA1c 7.0-10.5%, **established CVD or CKD**; **317 sites, 16 countries**; median follow-up **2 years**.
**MACE-4** (CV death, MI, stroke, unstable-angina admission): **4.2% vs 5.0%**; **HR 0.84** (0.59-1.20): **non-inferior** (margin 1.8; p<0.0001).
**Gastrointestinal adverse events**: **62.1% vs 14.2%**, the main reason for stopping orforglipron.
**Clinically significant or severe hypoglycaemia**: **6.8% vs 19.2%** (less with orforglipron).
**Deaths**: **1.4% vs 3.2%** (19 vs 43); all but one (in the glargine arm) were judged unrelated to treatment.
Caveat: a **safety** (non-inferiority) design, not proof of CV benefit; open-label; funded by **Eli Lilly**.
